title: Decentralize lint config into per-team profiles and add legacy-makefile compatibility shim
author: Maya Patel
description:
Motivation: Our single global lint/test matrix is driving long presubmit feedback and noisy failures for unrelated teams. Several services still rely on legacy Makefile targets that bootstrap heavy toolchains in CI which inflates setup times and flakiness. This PR aims to: 1) decentralize lint configuration into explicit per-team profiles under .ci/lint-profiles.yaml so teams can opt-in to stricter or lenient rules without touching global CI; 2) add a lightweight compatibility shim that executes legacy Makefile test targets inside a hermetic container (tools/ci-runner/compat_shim) to avoid duplicating global bootstrap steps; 3) introduce a fastpath presubmit lane that only runs surface-level checks (format, basic typecheck, unit smoke) and pushes full lint/type/integration to a staged presubmit or nightly job; 4) bump a few dev dependencies (eslint -> 9.17.0, typescript -> 5.4.x) and add an automated lockfile-regeneration check on release branches to prevent drift. The description below summarizes the changes, rationale, and rollout plan.

Design details: The new .ci/lint-profiles.yaml maps repo paths (or teams) to a named profile. CI templates pick the profile based on changed files and set environment variables for the lint runner. Profiles are small YAML blobs (ruleset, allowed-errors, skip-patterns). The compatibility shim wraps make targets in a containerized environment and exposes a minimal contract (exit codes, artifact dir) so existing Makefiles require zero changes. The fastpath lane is opt-in per repo via the same profile file.

Rollout plan: 1) Merge to main with feature flagged fastpath=false cluster-wide. 2) Enable per-team profiles for a small set of repos (redwood-serving, redwood-sdk-python, redwood-docs) for two weeks. 3) Flip fastpath=true for low-risk repos, monitor premerge times and flaky counts via CI telemetry. 4) Gradually onboard teams and clean up obsolete Makefile bootstraps.

Risks & mitigations: eslint/TS bumps could surface new warnings. We included a codemod script (tools/ci-scripts/eslint-codemods/convert-opts.js) and a temporary suppressions whitelist per-profile. The shim increases hermeticity but adds an extra binary (docker-wrapper); we added health checks and retry logic.

Checklist: - [x] Add .ci/lint-profiles.yaml and loader in CI templates - [x] Implement compat shim (Go) and unit tests - [x] Fastpath lane template + telemetry hooks - [x] Devdep bump + codemod + lockfile check - [x] Docs in docs/ci/team-lint-profiles.md

Related: ENG-2145 (reduce CI presubmit time), ENG-2212 (legacy-service-onboarding), SUP-4321 (customer incident flagged flaky presubmit)

review_thread:
Lucas Chen: Can we avoid bumping ESLint and TS in the same PR? If codemods are non-trivial they might delay rollout.
Maya Patel: Agree, I split codemod run into opt-in step and included suppressions; the bump is required to use new rule sets in strict profiles. Happy to split if reviewers prefer.
Nora Alvarez: compat_shim looks good but please add timeout guards and a cleanup handler for ephemeral containers.
Maya Patel: Added timeout + cleanup in adapter.go and unit test.
Devon Brooks: Fastpath lane metrics look useful — can we add a histogram of presubmit latency buckets?
Maya Patel: Added telemetry hook to emit latency buckets; will wire dashboards in a follow-up.
Lucas Chen (approve): Approving with the caveat we'll monitor eslint rule churn closely and may cut a hotfix if regressions appear.
ci_checks: Initial CI run: lint failed (ESLint errors from legacy code), unit tests passed. Second run after codemod + temporary suppressions: all checks passed. Summary: 12/12 checks green (build, go-unit, js-unit, eslint, ts-typecheck, presubmit-fastpath smoke). Nightly integration job unaffected.
merge_outcome: Merged via squash on 2026-02-01 by Maya Patel. Commit message summarizes profile mapping, compat shim, fastpath lane, and devdep bumps. No post-merge hotfixes required in the 72h window.
release_notes: - Add per-team lint profiles (.ci/lint-profiles.yaml) allowing targeted rule sets and opt-in fastpath presubmit lanes. - Add a hermetic compat shim to run legacy Makefile targets in CI without global bootstrap. - Introduce presubmit fastpath lane to reduce noise and speed feedback. - Bump dev dependencies (eslint 9.x, typescript 5.4); include codemod and temporary suppressions. - Add lockfile-regeneration check for release branches.
post_merge_actions: 1) Monitor CI presubmit latency and flaky counts for two weeks (telemetry dashboard: ci.presubmit.latency). 2) Reach out to teams with >10% suppressed ESLint rules to run codemod. 3) Schedule a follow-up to wire dashboards and opt-in onboarding sessions.
notes_for_release_manager: No behavioral changes to runtime or production artifacts. CI-only changes except devdep bumps; ensure release pipeline runs lockfile-regeneration step on next draft release. If eslint/TS-related regressions occur, revert the devdep bump-only commit and reintroduce codemods incrementally.
ci_impact_summary: Presubmit median time reduced from 6m30s to 2m10s on opted-in repos. Full presubmit still runs for critical repos; nightly job retains full checks. Fastpath reduces repeated lint churn for large monorepo PRs.
audit_trail: PR created 2026-01-19 by Maya Patel; review approvals by Lucas Chen and Nora Alvarez; merged 2026-02-01. CI green after one rerun following codemod/suppresses. Post-merge monitoring tasks created in ENG-2145.
